artworks.title: Tydeus, Hippomedon, and Parthenopaeus
artworks.description: Printed trio of Argive champions names Hippomedon among the Seven against Thebes — the Oncaidian-gate warrior of Apollodorus, standing with Tydeus and Parthenopaeus. Schoolbook imagery kept the lesser-sung chief visible beside Capaneus and Polynices.

artworks.title: The Seven Chiefs before Thebes
artworks.description: Mongez’s neoclassical machine gathers the Seven before the walls — Hippomedon among the oath-bound captains of Aeschylus and Statius. Salon ambition makes the Argive siege a single painted roster.

artworks.title: The Oath of the Seven Chiefs
artworks.description: Book illustration of the Seven swearing over the bull’s blood — Hippomedon’s cohort sealed for the Theban war. Popular engraving carried the Aeschylean oath into Victorian myth handbooks.

popCulture.title: Seven against Thebes
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus posts Hippomedon at a Theban gate among the Seven — the Argive chief whose death is part of the doomed assault.
